name: Idli with Sambar
cuisine: South Indian (Tamil Nadu / Karnataka, Udupi tiffin style)

ingredients.name: Urad dal (whole or split skinned black gram)
Oil (any neutral oil), to grease the idli plate
Toor dal (split pigeon pea, arhar dal)
Water (to cook dal, then to thin sambar)
Pumpkin (red/yellow pumpkin, kaddu) or bottle gourd (lauki)
Tamarind (imli)
ingredients.householdMeasure: a small marble-sized piece (about 1/2 tsp packed)

ingredients.name: Jaggery (gud), optional
ingredients.householdMeasure: a small pinch, about 1/2 tsp grated

equipment: Mixer-grinder with a wet/chutney jar, or a wet grinder (fluffiest idlis)
2 small bowls for soaking, and 1 large steel or glass bowl for fermenting (the batter rises 1.5-2 times)
Idli stand (idli plates) with an idli steamer, or an idli stand inside a pressure cooker (lid on, whistle removed)
Pressure cooker for the dal (a small steel bowl inside works for 20 g)
Saucepan or small kadai for the sambar, and a small tadka pan (or ladle) for tempering
Small bowl for soaking tamarind, a spoon to scoop idlis, a whisk or ladle to mash the dal
Knife, chopping board, measuring spoons, kitchen scale

steps.title: Measure 40 g idli rice into a bowl
steps.text: (smallest practical batch: 200 g).
steps.visualCue: short, thick, opaque grains, level at 40 g on the scale
steps.cameraCheck: the bowl of rice on the scale.
steps.videoShot: rice poured into a bowl on a kitchen scale.
steps.watchOut: scooping by cup, which gives too much rice and a stiff batter; weigh it or use 3 level tbsp.

steps.title: Rinse the rice 3 times in fresh water
steps.text: , rubbing it gently between your fingers.
steps.visualCue: the first water is thick and white, the third is thin and almost clear
steps.cameraCheck: the bowl with the last rinse water.
steps.videoShot: a hand swirling rice, then the cloudy water poured off.
steps.watchOut: skipping the rinse, which leaves surface starch and a gummy batter; keep rinsing until the water is faintly cloudy.

steps.title: Cover the rice with water about 3 cm above the grains
steps.text: Add the 2 g poha now if using.
steps.visualCue: a clear layer of water about two finger-widths above the rice
steps.cameraCheck: the bowl from the side, showing the water level.
steps.videoShot: water poured over the rice.
steps.watchOut: grains poking out, which stay hard and grind unevenly; top up with water until covered.

steps.title: Measure 10 g urad dal and a small pinch of fenugreek seeds into a second bowl
steps.text: (batch: 50 g dal + 1/4 tsp methi).
steps.visualCue: white dal with a few yellow seeds mixed in
steps.cameraCheck: the bowl with white dal and a few yellow seeds.
steps.videoShot: dal and methi dropped into a bowl.
steps.watchOut: too much methi, which makes the idlis bitter; keep to a pinch.

steps.title: Rinse the dal twice, then cover it with water 3 cm above
steps.text: Rinse the dal twice, then cover it with water 3 cm above
steps.tip: soak and grind the dal separately from the rice. Whipped-up urad dal is what makes idlis light.
steps.visualCue: the second rinse water is only slightly cloudy and the dal sits fully covered
steps.cameraCheck: the soaking bowl.
steps.videoShot: dal rinsed and topped up with water.
steps.watchOut: old or stale dal (more than a year old), which ferments poorly and gives flat idlis; use fresh dal or add a little more.

steps.title: Leave both bowls covered for 4-5 hours
steps.text: Leave both bowls covered for 4-5 hours
steps.visualCue: swollen, plump dal and rice grains that no longer look glassy
steps.cameraCheck: one rice grain pressed between two fingers.
steps.videoShot: a soaked grain crushed between fingertips.
steps.watchOut: soaking in a hot place, which turns the water sour before grinding; keep it at room temperature and change the water if it smells off.

steps.title: Drain the urad dal (keep the soaking water) and put it in the mixer jar
steps.text: Drain the urad dal (keep the soaking water) and put it in the mixer jar
steps.visualCue: damp white dal in the jar and a bowl of cloudy water beside it
steps.cameraCheck: the jar with drained dal.
steps.videoShot: dal tipped from a sieve into the jar.
steps.watchOut: throwing away the soaking water, which you need for grinding; keep it.

steps.title: Add 1 tbsp cold soaking water and grind in 20-second bursts for about 2 min
steps.text: Scrape the sides, add 1 more tbsp, and grind 1-2 min more.
steps.visualCue: pale, fluffy, doubled-in-volume batter that holds a soft peak on the spoon
steps.cameraCheck: a spoon of dal batter dropped into water, floating.
steps.videoShot: fluffy white batter lifted on a spoon.
steps.watchOut: a hot jar from continuous grinding, which makes the batter heavy and the idlis dense; use short bursts and cold water, and rest the jar if it feels warm.

steps.title: Scrape the dal batter into the large fermenting bowl
steps.text: Scrape the dal batter into the large fermenting bowl
steps.visualCue: a high, airy mound of white batter in a bowl big enough to double
steps.cameraCheck: the fermenting bowl.
steps.videoShot: batter scraped into a big steel bowl.
steps.watchOut: a small bowl, which overflows when the batter rises; choose one at least 3 times the batter volume.

steps.title: Drain the rice (and poha) and grind with about 1-2 tbsp water for 2-3 min
steps.text: Drain the rice (and poha) and grind with about 1-2 tbsp water for 2-3 min
steps.tip: idli rice batter should be a little coarser than dosa batter.
steps.visualCue: thick, creamy batter that feels like fine sand when rubbed
steps.cameraCheck: a little rice batter rubbed on a fingertip.
steps.videoShot: thick, slightly grainy rice batter pouring from the jar.
steps.watchOut: grinding too smooth, which gives sticky, gummy idlis; stop as soon as it is fine but still grainy.

steps.title: Add the rice batter to the dal batter, add 1.2 g salt (batch: 1 tsp), and mix with your clean hand for 1 min
steps.text: Add the rice batter to the dal batter, add 1.2 g salt (batch: 1 tsp), and mix with your clean hand for 1 min
steps.visualCue: one uniform off-white batter with no streaks
steps.cameraCheck: batter dripping slowly from a spoon.
steps.videoShot: a hand folding the two batters together.
steps.watchOut: mixing with a metal spoon for too long, which knocks out air; fold gently, and use clean hands (their natural yeast helps fermenting). Some cooks add the salt after fermenting instead; both work.

steps.title: Cover loosely and leave in a warm spot for 8-12 hours
steps.text: (overnight).
steps.tip: in Mumbai summer check at 6-8 h; in winter it may need 14 h or more. Judge by the rise and smell, not the clock.
steps.visualCue: a domed top with bubbles breaking at the surface and a faint sour-yeasty smell
steps.cameraCheck: the bowl from the side, showing the risen level and bubbles.
steps.videoShot: a spoon dipped into airy, bubbly batter.
steps.watchOut: cold weather (little or no rise) or a tight lid (no room for gas); move the bowl somewhere warmer, leave the lid loose, and wait longer rather than adding anything.

steps.title: Rinse 20 g toor dal twice and put it in a small steel bowl with 100 ml water and a pinch of turmeric
steps.text: Rinse 20 g toor dal twice and put it in a small steel bowl with 100 ml water and a pinch of turmeric
steps.visualCue: pale-yellow dal with a yellow tinge from the turmeric under about 2 cm of water
steps.cameraCheck: the bowl of dal and water.
steps.videoShot: yellow dal rinsed and topped with water.
steps.watchOut: too little water, which burns or leaves the dal hard; keep the water about 2 cm above the dal.

steps.title: Pressure-cook the dal (bowl inside the cooker with 1 cup water at the base) for 3-4 whistles on medium heat
steps.text: Let the pressure drop on its own.
steps.visualCue: the dal collapses into a thick yellow mush when pressed
steps.cameraCheck: a spoon pressing the cooked dal.
steps.videoShot: the cooker lid opened and dal mashed.
steps.watchOut: opening the cooker early, which is unsafe and leaves hard dal; wait until the steam stops. If the dal is still firm, cook 1-2 more whistles.

steps.title: While the dal cooks, soak 3 g tamarind in 2 tbsp hot water
steps.text: While the dal cooks, soak 3 g tamarind in 2 tbsp hot water
steps.visualCue: the pulp loosens and the water turns brown
steps.cameraCheck: the tamarind in the small bowl.
steps.videoShot: hot water poured over tamarind.
steps.watchOut: using boiling-hot water on a big piece, which takes forever to soften; break the piece up with a spoon.

steps.title: Peel 4-5 shallots and halve the larger ones. Cut the drumstick into 5 cm pieces, and cube the carrot and pumpkin. Chop the tomato
steps.text: Peel 4-5 shallots and halve the larger ones. Cut the drumstick into 5 cm pieces, and cube the carrot and pumpkin. Chop the tomato
steps.visualCue: even 1.5 cm cubes that will cook at the same speed
steps.cameraCheck: the board with all the cut vegetables.
steps.videoShot: drumstick being cut into pieces.
steps.watchOut: very uneven pieces, so some turn to mush while others stay raw; cut carrot smaller than pumpkin.

steps.title: Squeeze the soaked tamarind with your fingers and strain the juice. Throw away the fibre and seeds
steps.text: Squeeze the soaked tamarind with your fingers and strain the juice. Throw away the fibre and seeds
steps.visualCue: a thin brown liquid with no seeds or strings
steps.cameraCheck: the strained tamarind water.
steps.videoShot: tamarind squeezed and poured through a strainer.
steps.watchOut: seeds slipping into the pot, which crack teeth; strain through a small sieve.

steps.title: Mash the cooked dal smooth with a whisk or the back of a ladle
steps.text: Mash the cooked dal smooth with a whisk or the back of a ladle
steps.visualCue: smooth, glossy, thick yellow dal
steps.cameraCheck: the mashed dal.
steps.videoShot: dal whisked smooth.
steps.watchOut: lumps, which make the sambar grainy; whisk until smooth, adding a spoon of water if stiff.

steps.title: Put the shallots, drumstick, carrot and pumpkin in the saucepan with 100 ml water and a pinch of salt. Cover and cook on medium heat
steps.text: Put the shallots, drumstick, carrot and pumpkin in the saucepan with 100 ml water and a pinch of salt. Cover and cook on medium heat
steps.visualCue: soft but whole vegetables, drumstick skin slightly wrinkled
steps.cameraCheck: a carrot cube pierced with a knife.
steps.videoShot: the lid lifted on simmering vegetables.
steps.watchOut: overcooking until everything dissolves; test at 6 min and stop as soon as the knife slides in.

steps.title: Add the tomato, the tamarind water and 1 1/2 tsp sambar powder. Simmer
steps.text: Add the tomato, the tamarind water and 1 1/2 tsp sambar powder. Simmer
steps.visualCue: the liquid turns reddish-brown and smells roasted and tangy
steps.cameraCheck: the reddish-brown liquid in the pan.
steps.videoShot: sambar powder sprinkled in and stirred.
steps.watchOut: adding the powder to a dry hot pan, where it scorches and turns bitter; always add it to the liquid.

steps.title: Add the mashed dal, 1/4 tsp salt (minus the pinch already added) and the jaggery (optional). Stir, add a splash of water if too thick, and simmer
steps.text: Add the mashed dal, 1/4 tsp salt (minus the pinch already added) and the jaggery (optional). Stir, add a splash of water if too thick, and simmer
steps.tip: tiffin sambar for idli is meant to be thin, so the idlis can soak it up. It thickens as it cools.
steps.visualCue: a pourable, lightly thick sambar that coats the back of a spoon thinly
steps.cameraCheck: a ladle of sambar poured back into the pan.
steps.videoShot: sambar flowing off a ladle.
steps.watchOut: a thick, pasty sambar, which does not soak into the idli; thin it with hot water. If too salty, add a little more water and dal.

steps.title: Heat 1 tsp oil in the tadka pan on medium heat. Add 1/4 tsp mustard seeds
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp oil in the tadka pan on medium heat. Add 1/4 tsp mustard seeds
steps.visualCue: seeds spluttering and jumping in the oil
steps.cameraCheck: the pan with popping seeds.
steps.videoShot: mustard seeds spluttering.
steps.watchOut: oil that is not hot enough, so the seeds do not pop and taste raw; wait for the first crackle before moving on.

steps.title: Add the broken red chilli, the curry leaves and a pinch of hing (optional)
steps.text: Add the broken red chilli, the curry leaves and a pinch of hing (optional)
steps.visualCue: curry leaves curling and crisp-looking, strong fragrance
steps.cameraCheck: the tadka in the pan.
steps.videoShot: curry leaves sizzling.
steps.watchOut: burnt chilli and leaves, which taste bitter; if they go black, start the tadka again. Keep the pan lid close, because wet leaves spit.

steps.title: Pour the tadka into the sambar, add the chopped coriander, stir and turn off the heat
steps.text: Keep it covered so it stays hot.
steps.visualCue: dark seeds and green leaves floating on the surface
steps.cameraCheck: the finished sambar with leaves and seeds on top.
steps.videoShot: the hot tadka hitting the sambar.
steps.watchOut: leaving the sambar uncovered, so it cools and forms a skin; keep it covered and reheat before serving.

steps.title: Pour about 3 cm of water into the idli steamer (or pressure cooker) and bring it to a boil on high heat
steps.text: Pour about 3 cm of water into the idli steamer (or pressure cooker) and bring it to a boil on high heat
steps.visualCue: a steady stream of steam from under the lid and rolling bubbles in the water
steps.cameraCheck: the steaming pot.
steps.videoShot: water bubbling in the steamer base.
steps.watchOut: water touching the idli plate, which makes soggy bottoms; keep the water below the stand.

steps.title: Grease 3 cups of the idli plate with a few drops of oil (about 1/4 tsp in total)
steps.text: Grease 3 cups of the idli plate with a few drops of oil (about 1/4 tsp in total)
steps.visualCue: a glossy film in each cup with no puddles
steps.cameraCheck: the greased idli plate.
steps.videoShot: a fingertip spreading oil in the moulds.
steps.watchOut: skipping the oil, so the idlis stick and tear; too much oil leaves oily patches.

steps.title: Gently stir the fermented batter once, without beating out the air
steps.text: Take out about 150 g (a heaped 2/3 cup) and refrigerate the rest.
steps.visualCue: bubbly batter that falls from the spoon in a slow ribbon
steps.cameraCheck: the batter in a cup.
steps.videoShot: batter scooped into a cup, showing bubbles.
steps.watchOut: vigorous stirring, which deflates the batter and gives flat idlis; fold only 3-4 times. A runny batter gives flat idlis, so add no water unless it is stiff.

steps.title: Fill each of the 3 cups to the brim, about 50 g batter each
steps.text: Fill each of the 3 cups to the brim, about 50 g batter each
steps.visualCue: batter level with the rim and a smooth top
steps.cameraCheck: the filled idli plate.
steps.videoShot: batter spooned into the moulds.
steps.watchOut: underfilling, which gives small flat idlis, or overfilling so they merge; fill level with the rim.

steps.title: Place the plate in the steamer, cover with the lid (pressure cooker: remove the whistle), and steam on medium-high heat
steps.text: Place the plate in the steamer, cover with the lid (pressure cooker: remove the whistle), and steam on medium-high heat
steps.visualCue: risen, pale, glossy domes and a clean toothpick
steps.cameraCheck: a toothpick pulled out of one idli.
steps.videoShot: the lid lifted, steam escaping from puffed idlis.
steps.watchOut: opening the lid in the first 8 minutes, which makes the idlis sink; if the toothpick has wet batter on it, steam 2 more minutes.

steps.title: Take out the plate and let it rest for 2-3 minutes
steps.text: Take out the plate and let it rest for 2-3 minutes
steps.visualCue: the surface looks matte and the edges lift away from the cup
steps.cameraCheck: the plate on the counter.
steps.videoShot: the idli plate resting.
steps.watchOut: unmoulding at once, which tears the soft idlis; wait the 2-3 minutes.

steps.title: Dip a spoon in water, slide it round the edge of each idli and lift it out
steps.text: Dip a spoon in water, slide it round the edge of each idli and lift it out
steps.visualCue: whole, spongy idlis with a smooth underside
steps.cameraCheck: the 3 idlis on a plate.
steps.videoShot: a wet spoon lifting out a clean idli.
steps.watchOut: a dry spoon, which sticks and tears the idli; keep dipping it in water.

steps.title: Serve the idlis with a bowl of hot sambar poured beside or over them
steps.text: (and coconut chutney if you like).
steps.visualCue: white idlis sitting in or beside steaming reddish sambar
steps.cameraCheck: the full plate.
steps.videoShot: hot sambar ladled over soft idlis.
steps.watchOut: cold sambar or idlis left to dry out; serve both piping hot, and cover idlis with a cloth if waiting.

reasons: idlis are steamed, not fried, and fermentation makes them easy to digest. The home plate uses only about 1 1/4 tsp oil in total (saturated fat about 1.2 g), and the sambar adds dal protein, fibre (about 9 g) and four vegetables. Points are lost because it is mostly white rice (about 66 g carbs) with modest protein (about 12 g), and salt is about 2.7 g (54% of the 5 g limit). Restaurant sambar is often oilier, sometimes sweetened, and served with generous coconut chutney, which pushes up fat and salt.

researchRating.basis: idli sambar is one of India's most-ordered and most-praised breakfasts. Swiggy has reported millions of idli orders a year (Outlook Business coverage), and Mumbai guides (LBB, The Infatuation, Homegrown, Curly Tales, Culture Trip) single out Matunga idli as worth the trip. It loses some points because some see it as plain or "everyday", and flat, hard or sour idlis are a very common home problem (recipe sites devote long troubleshooting sections to soft idlis). TasteAtlas rating: Not found in search results, so not used. A May 2026 Reddit thread still recommends Matunga idli places, so sentiment is unchanged.

storage: Idlis: fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 2 days. They freeze well for up to 1 month (freeze on a plate, then bag). Reheat by steaming for 3-5 min (from frozen, 8-10 min), or microwave with a damp cloth over them for 30-60 sec. Sambar: fridge-safe for 2-3 days in a closed container; it can be frozen for up to 1 month. Reheat in a pan until boiling, adding a splash of water as it thickens. Batter: fridge for 3-4 days (it gets more sour each day; use older batter for dosa or uttapam). Can be frozen for up to 1 month; thaw in the fridge and stir.
leftoverRemix: turn leftover idlis into idli upma or masala fried idli. Cut them into cubes, toss in a pan with a mustard-curry leaf tempering, onion, a pinch of turmeric and a sprinkle of podi or sambar powder, and finish with lemon and coriander. Leftover sambar can be poured over the cubes for "sambar idli bites".
burnOff: about 5.6 km of running (70 kg adult, about 70 kcal per km), or about 7.8 km of brisk walking (est., about 50 kcal per km). With 2 tbsp coconut chutney (about 475 kcal): about 6.8 km running or about 9.5 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: rice, urad dal, toor dal and shallots are not eaten on the common vrat rule set (grains and pulses avoided, assumption used)

ekadashi.reason: rice and pulses are avoided on Ekadashi in the common rule set (assumption used)

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; light and easy to digest, but carb-heavy with modest protein, so add extra dal in the sambar for sehri
